::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
**Planned strand.** This page shows the direction for these lessons. They are not written yet.
:::

**The big idea:** students look beyond the classroom: where computer science research is heading, how it works with other fields, and what education and careers it leads to. Instead of a separate unit, these are short lessons placed between modules, each tied to the module just finished, plus a research report submitted in stages.

**Expectations:** D2.1, D2.2, D2.3, D3.1, D3.2, D3.3, D3.4, D3.5

## Planned Lessons

| When | Lesson | Focus |
|---|---|---|
| After Module 2 | Who Builds Computers? | Careers in hardware, support, and software, locally, nationally, and internationally (D3.1); Essential Skills and work habits from the Ontario Skills Passport (D3.5) |
| After Module 3 | Faster Than One Computer | Parallel processing and distributed computing (D2.1); choosing a research topic |
| After Module 4 | Security as a Career | Cryptography and security research (D2.1); experiential learning: co-op, job shadowing, competitions, career fairs (D3.2) |
| After Module 5 | Computer Science + Another Field | Collaborative research, e.g., health informatics, climatology, or bioinformatics (D2.2); supports for non-traditional career choices (D3.4) |
| After Module 6 | Where Next? | College and university programs, certifications, entrance requirements, and costs (D3.3); research report presentations (D2.3) |

## Research Report (Planned)

Students research one emerging area of computer science (for example, artificial intelligence, computer vision, cryptography, robotics, or human–computer interaction) and its link to another field. It is submitted in stages: topic and sources, notes and outline, then a final report in a format of the student's choice (website, slide presentation, or video). Where possible, students connect the topic to the kind of computer and network they have studied in the course.
